learning_outcomes.text: Students will have a broad and integrated knowledge and understanding of Electromagnetic Compatibility. They will describe the coupling mechanisms in EMC and be able to explain the remedial measures.
Students will have detailed knowledge for identifying electromagnetic coupling mechanisms and selecting appropriate measures to reduce interference.

Students will apply a range of standard and some advanced procedures and methods to obtain information on electromagnetic interference. Software for calculating electromagnetic fields will be used to solve EMC problems.
Students will recognize potential EMC problems of technical systems in advance and solve them by systematically applying learned strategies. A technical-economic optimum will be sought.
Students will analyze EMC problems, identify coupling mechanisms, recognize weaknesses in electrical systems, and propose solutions. They will clearly present the results of their calculations.

syllabus_topics: Sources of interference and disturbing variables
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam, as specified in the applicable study regulations. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 4 experiments.
